events.label: Death of William the Conqueror
events.note: Died at Rouen after injuries and illness following the Mantes campaign.

notes: Central figure for the Norman conquest family tree MVP. Birth year is approximate.

deathCause.summary: Died from illness and injuries after campaign
deathCause.detail: William died at Rouen in 1087 after becoming seriously ill following the Mantes campaign. His death is usually treated as campaign-related illness or injury rather than assassination.

notes: Father of William the Conqueror. Birth year is approximate.

events.label: Death of Robert Curthose
events.note: Died while imprisoned at Cardiff Castle.

notes: Eldest son of William the Conqueror. Birth year is approximate.

deathCause.summary: Died in captivity at Cardiff Castle
deathCause.detail: Robert Curthose died in 1134 after many years imprisoned by his brother Henry I. The death itself is not usually treated as murder, but the long captivity is central to the context.

events.label: Death in the New Forest
events.note: Killed by an arrow while hunting. Walter Tirel is traditionally named, though intent remains disputed.

notes: Third son of William the Conqueror. Birth year is approximate.

deathCause.summary: Killed by an arrow; intent disputed
deathCause.detail: William II was shot by an arrow in the New Forest on 2 August 1100. Walter Tirel is traditionally identified as the archer, but whether this was accident, negligence, or murder remains disputed.

events.label: Death of Henry I
events.note: Traditionally linked to illness after eating too many lampreys.

notes: Youngest son of William the Conqueror. Birth year is approximate.

deathCause.detail: Henry I died in Normandy in 1135 after a sudden illness, traditionally said to have followed eating lampreys against medical advice.

events.label: Death of Henry II
events.note: Died at Chinon after illness during war with Philip II and Richard.

deathCause.detail: Henry II died at Chinon in 1189 after falling ill during his final conflict with Philip II of France and his son Richard. This was not a violent death, but the political collapse around it was severe.
